injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Isaiah Bond
injuries.headline: Bond (concussion) has cleared protocol and is practicing Monday, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
injuries.notes: Bond was concussed in Cleveland's second preseason game and was nearing 100 percent at the end of August. He's expected to fill the WR4 role for the Browns behind KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy. As a rookie last season, Bond caught just 18 of 44 targets for 338 yards and zero touchdowns as a deep threat.

injuries.name: Sam Williams
injuries.headline: The Browns are set to sign Williams to their active roster, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys in early March but was waived Sunday. He compiled 9.5 regular-season sacks over his first two years in the league but missed all of 2024 due to a knee injury and recorded just 1.0 sacks despite logging a career-high 469 defensive snaps last year. Williams will look to get back on track in what is likely to be a rotational role with the Browns this season.

injuries.name: Kalia Davis
injuries.headline: The Browns placed Davis on injured reserve Tuesday due to a quadriceps injury.
injuries.notes: Davis sustained the injury during a training camp practice in late July, forcing him to miss all three of the Browns' preseason games. By opening the regular season on IR, the fifth-year defensive tackle will be required to miss at least four games, so Week 5 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11 is the earliest the Davis can see the field. Adin Huntington and Mike Hall will serve as the Browns' rotational options at defensive tackle behind starters Mason Graham and Maliek Collins for as long as Davis is sidelined.

injuries.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuries.headline: Turpin returned five kickoffs for 122 yards and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Turpin only saw eight offensive snaps on the night, recording his only catch in that small window of opportunity. However, Turpin made his usual impact on special teams, helping the Dallas offense garner solid starting field position all evening.

injuries.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuries.headline: Mingo caught his sole target for 10 yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Mingo played 11 of 58 offensive snaps and six special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver seems to be getting mixed in on snaps when CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens or Ryan Flournoy need a break. Mingo remains the fifth option for the Cowboys wide-receiver corps and will likely continue to see minimal opportunities in a highly competitive room.

injuries.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuries.headline: Schoonmaker finished with one catch for 12 yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: The tight end played on 13 of 58 offensive snaps and 10 more on special teams. Schoonmaker, now in his fourth NFL season, has 50 career catches in the regular season.

injuries.name: Emari Demercado
injuries.headline: Demercado recorded two carries for seven yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Demercado operated as the team's No. 2 option at running back Week 1 behind starter Javonte Williams, but he was limited to just five snaps on offense in the contest. Demercado was claimed off waivers by Dallas on Aug. 31, and his role could grow as he continues to get more comfortable in the Cowboys offense moving forward, especially with Malik Davis (hip) out for the season.

injuries.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
injuries.headline: Spann-Ford caught both of his targets for 14 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Spann-Ford is the No. 2 tight end behind Jake Ferguson, but the secondary option outperformed Ferguson by eight receiving yards in Sunday's contest. Spann-Ford played 13 offensive snaps and 11 special-teams snaps, contributing to the Cowboys in both phases to the start the season.

injuries.name: Hunter Luepke
injuries.headline: Luepke turned his only carry into a seven-yard gain during Sunday night's 28-20 loss to New York.
injuries.notes: Luepke operated in his typical role as the team's starting fullback, seeing action for 15 of the team's 58 total offensive snaps. The 26-year-old also was on the field for nine snaps on special teams in contest. Luepke is a far more valuable real-life football player than he is a fantasy asset.

injuries.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuries.headline: Flournoy caught two of four targets for 22 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Flournoy started the contest, playing 41 of the team's 58 offensive snaps while operating as the No. 3 wide receiver behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Flournoy saw four or more targets only five times over 16 regular-season contests in 2025, and he'll have a limited ceiling as a fantasy asset as long as Pickens and Lamb are available.

injuries.name: Jake Ferguson
injuries.headline: Ferguson caught both of his targets for six yards during Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Ferguson along with quarterback Dak Prescott, amongst others, did not play during the preseason, and the team never really got into a groove on offense Week 1. The tight end remains the unquestioned No. 1 option at his position with Dallas, and he'll have a chance to be more involved Week 2 against Washington.

injuries.name: DeMarvion Overshown
injuries.headline: Coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Overshown is expected to miss 1-to-2 weeks due to the hamstring injury he sustained during Sunday's loss against the Giants, Andrew Siciliano of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: Overshown was forced out of the Cowboys' regular-season opener early with a hamstring issue, and it seems like he'll likely have to sit out at least one game as he recovers. Any time he spends on the sidelines could open up additional time at linebacker for rookie third-round pick Jaishawn Barham.

injuries.name: Malik Hooker
injuries.headline: Hooker was diagnosed with a forearm fracture after undergoing tests Monday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: The safety left Sunday's loss to the Giants in the fourth quarter and did not return. He seems likely to miss at least two weeks, according to Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News.  P.J. Locke and Markquese Bell would be the next two up at safety if Hooker has to sit for an extended period.

injuries.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuries.headline: Aubrey made just two of three extra-point attempts in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: The big-legged kicker didn't attempt a field goal against New York. His missed PAT came after a Javonte Williams touchdown in which he also picked up a taunting penalty to push Aubrey's extra-point try back to a 48-yard attempt. Widely drafted as the top kicker in fantasy this summer, Aubrey's Week 1 was less than ideal. He finished as fantasy's No. 4 overall kicker in points per game last season.

injuries.name: Dak Prescott
injuries.headline: Prescott completed 22 of 34 passes for 175 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants. He also rushed twice for 14 yards.
injuries.notes: Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb for a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter and found Javonte Williams for a 17-yard touchdown in the fourth. Prescott's interception in the final minute of the first half proved costly, as the Giants scored a go-ahead touchdown six plays later and led the rest of the way. Lamb finished with just 44 yards and George Pickens had only 28, as Dallas' talented passing game was stuck in first gear. Prescott, who finished third in the league with 4,552 passing yards during the 2025 regular season, will try to pick up the pace in Dallas' Week 2 home opener against the Commanders.

injuries.name: Javonte Williams
injuries.headline: Williams rushed 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Williams scored a one-yard rushing touchdown in the third quarter and added a 17-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. He was called for a 15-yard taunting penalty on his touchdown catch, and Brandon Aubrey missed the ensuing PAT to keep Dallas' deficit at eight points with 5:21 remaining, though that miss proved moot after the Giants proceeded to eat up the remainder of the game clock on the ensuing possession. No Cowboys teammate had more than two carries in Sunday's loss, so Williams is locked in as the primary option in Dallas' backfield heading into a Week 2 home game against the Commanders.

injuries.name: George Pickens
injuries.headline: Pickens caught three of six targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Pickens had a couple drops in Sunday night's underwhelming season-opening performance. He was also quiet Week 1 last season with a 30-yard receiving performance against the Eagles, but Pickens went on to post career highs with 1,429 receiving yards and nine TDs during the 2025 regular season. The talented wide receiver has a nice rebound opportunity coming up Week 2 against a Washington secondary that was among the league's leakiest in 2025.

injuries.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuries.headline: Lamb caught five of eight targets for 44 yards and a touchdown while adding one carry for no gain in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
injuries.notes: Lamb led the team in targets and receiving yards, as Dak Prescott threw for only 175 yards in a subpar Week 1 showing from Dallas' talented passing game. It was encouraging to see Lamb find the end zone in the season opener after he scored a career-low three touchdowns across 14 appearances during the 2025 regular season. Lamb had at least six total TDs in each of the preceding five campaigns, and he got on the board with a one-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter against the Giants. The Cowboys will aim to bounce back in their Week 2 home opener against the Commanders.

injuries.name: Malik Davis
injuries.headline: The Cowboys placed Davis (hip) on injured reserve Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Davis underwent surgery Saturday for a hip injury, and Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports that the procedure will sideline the 27-year-old running back for the entire 2026 season. With Davis on the shelf, the Cowboys bolstered their backfield depth by signing Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster, with the latter serving as the RB3 behind Javonte Williams and Emari Demercado.

injuries.name: Tyler Guyton
injuries.headline: Guyton (elbow) wasn't listed on Dallas' injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Guyton was dealing with elbow soreness last month but is now healthy again. The 2024 first-round pick is expected to serve as the Cowboys' starting left tackle once the regular season gets underway.

injuries.name: Jonathan Bullard
injuries.headline: Bullard (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Bullard was limited to side work during most of training camp and did not play in any of the Cowboys' three preseason games while recovering from a hamstring injury in early August. The rehab work has evidently paid off, and the veteran nose tackle is on track to play in Sunday's regular-season opener against the Giants. Bullard appeared in 15 regular-season games for the Saints in 2025, finishing with 26 tackles (12 solo) and two pass defenses.

injuries.name: Tyler Smith
injuries.headline: The Cowboys placed Smith (thumb) on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Smith is scheduled to miss four to six weeks to recover from a procedure on his injured thumb. He'll be required to miss at least the Cowboys' next four games, so the earliest that the fifth-year offensive lineman can play is Week 5 against the Buccaneers on Thursday, Oct. 8. T.J. Bass will serve as the Cowboys' starting left guard for as long as Smith is sidelined.

injuries.notes: ir

injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Bo Nix
injuries.headline: Nix completed 17 of 28 passes for 131 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding three carries for two yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night. He also committed three fumbles, losing one and recovering one of the two others that remained with Denver.
injuries.notes: Nix's season and night immediately got off on the wrong foot when he threw an ill-advised interception into blanket coverage on the part of rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) on the Broncos' opening drive of 2026, setting up the Chiefs' first touchdown of the night. When Nix wasn't turning the ball over -- he also lost the handle on a late third-quarter sack to give Kansas City possession at the Broncos' 34-yard line -- he was having significant trouble producing any noteworthy gains with his arm, averaging just 4.7 yards per attempt overall. Nix did connect with Evan Engram in the first quarter for a 19-yard scoring strike that answered the Chiefs' first touchdown, but he'll have plenty of room for improvement in a Week 2 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday.

injuries.name: Courtland Sutton
injuries.headline: Sutton secured two of five targets for 11 yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Sutton, along with the rest of the Broncos offense, endured a miserable night, and the veteran receiver tied for the second-fewest receptions and third-fewest yards among Denver pass catchers to record at least one grab. Sutton also was the intended receiver on Bo Nix's early-game interception, making it an all-around throwaway season-opening performance. Sutton's first chance to atone comes in Denver's Week 2 home opener Sunday, which sees a talented Jaguars team come into the Mile High City.

injuries.name: RJ Harvey
injuries.headline: Harvey rushed three times for 18 yards, brought in all four targets for 23 yards and returned four kickoffs for 111 yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Harvey saw an uptick in opportunities as a pass catcher due to game script, one that saw the Broncos fall behind by a 24-10 margin late in the third quarter. The second-year back also was efficient with his trio of carries, which were five fewer than those logged by lead runner J.K. Dobbins. Harvey should have a chance for more opportunities on the ground in most games this season, including a Week 2 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday where Denver's offense will have a higher probability of running a more balanced attack.

injuries.name: J.K. Dobbins
injuries.headline: Dobbins rushed eight times for 36 yards and wasn't targeted in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
injuries.notes: The highlight of Dobbins' relatively unremarkable night came early in the third quarter, when he changed direction shortly after taking the handoff and rumbled around left end for a 17-yard gain. The veteran back otherwise found running room difficult to come by against a dominant Chiefs defense, and Dobbins' rushing opportunities were notably limited overall due to game script. There will be much more cohesive offensive performances for the Broncos this season, and Dobbins should be in line for a bigger workload during Denver's home opener Week 2 against the Jaguars.

injuries.name: Jaylen Waddle
injuries.headline: Waddle brought in one of three targets for two yards in the Broncos' 31-10 loss to the Chiefs on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Waddle's regular-season Broncos debut was as miserable as his final line suggests, as the prominent offseason addition finished last in receptions and yards among Denver players that recorded at least one catch. One of the two targets Waddle couldn't corral was a key third-down drop early in the third quarter, although he was hardly the only underwhelming component of a pass-catching corps that produced a modest 131 total receiving yards. More productive performances are surely ahead for Waddle and the Broncos' air attack, with the first opportunity for atonement coming in a Week 2 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday.

injuries.name: Marvin Mims Jr.
injuries.headline: Mims (hip) has re-entered Monday's Week 1 matchup against the Chiefs, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
injuries.notes: Mims exited to the locker room in the first quarter and was deemed questionable to return by Denver. However, he was back on the sideline shortly thereafter, then came back into the contest during a punt return. Mims thus should be good to go for the remainder of the matchup unless he aggravates the issue or suffers another injury.

injuries.name: Adam Prentice
injuries.headline: The Broncos elevated Prentice from the practice squad ahead of Monday's game against the Chiefs, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Denver cut Prentice following the preseason, but the 29-year-old fullback will be temporarily added back to the roster in advance of Monday's season opener. Prentice suited up for all 17 games of the regular season with Denver in 2025, carrying 10 times for 44 yards and adding six receptions for 53 yards on eight targets.

injuries.name: Luke Wattenberg
injuries.headline: Wattenberg (undisclosed) was not listed on the Broncos' official injury report Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Wattenberg was dealing with an undisclosed injury during training camp, but he appears to be past it as Week 1 prep begins for the Broncos. He should resume his starting role at center Monday at Kansas City.

injuries.name: Riley Moss
injuries.headline: Moss (ribs) wasn't listed on the Broncos' injury report Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Moss dealt with an injury to his ribs at the end of August, but his absence from Denver's injury report Thursday suggests he's clear of the issue. He should thus be ready to start at cornerback in Monday's season opener against Kansas City.

injuries.name: Jonah Coleman
injuries.headline: Coleman is likely to serve as the Broncos' between-the-tackles complement to starter J.K. Dobbins this season, Nick Kosmider of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Coleman was selected in the fourth round of April's draft after completing his four-year college career with a 2025 campaign with Washington during which he compiled 758 yards and 15 touchdowns on 156 carries over 12 contests. He also added 31 catches for 354 yards and two scores during his senior season. The Huskies played with an up-tempo style, so Coleman was on the field for all downs, resulting in him becoming a capable receiver and pass blocker. The running back is considered a more physical back than RJ Harvey, who also is set to serve as a reserve option behind Dobbins this season, and as a result, Coleman could be ticketed to serve more frequently as a direct replacement for Dobbins.

injuries.name: Pat Bryant
injuries.headline: Bryant is slotted in as a top reserve option on the Broncos' unofficial depth chart.
injuries.notes: Bryant reeled in 31 of 49 targets for 378 yards and a touchdown over 15 regular-season contests in his rookie campaign with Denver in 2025. The 23-year-old possesses a 6-foot-2, 200-plus pound frame, and he's on track to operate as the immediate backup behind Courtland Sutton as a boundary receiver with Denver this season. Bryant has already impressed with his physicality at his position, and he could earn more opportunities in his first campaign with new play caller Davis Webb.

injuries.name: Jarrett Stidham
injuries.headline: Coach Sean Payton said Wednesday that Stidham will be the Broncos' backup quarterback to begin the 2026 season, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
injuries.notes: Sam Ehlinger pushed Stidham during training camp for his spot on Denver's depth chart behind starter Bo Nix, and the team opted to keep three quarterbacks on its initial 53-man roster, but at least for now, Stidham is second in the pecking order. Unless Nix gets hurt at some point, neither Stidham nor Ehlinger would be expected to get any snaps in a reasonably close game.

injuries.name: Jonathon Cooper
injuries.headline: Cooper pleaded not guilty to five charges of domestic violence in a Douglas County (Colo.) courtroom Monday, Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Cooper now has a jury trial scheduled to begin Nov. 10 following a pair of domestic incidents that occurred a week apart in early June. The NFL placed him on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Sunday, which means he still gets paid and can attend team meetings but can't practice or play in games. Cooper's stint on the list is indefinite but may last for as long as his legal situation is playing out in court.

injuries.name: Nick Gargiulo
injuries.headline: Gargiulo (knee) was moved to the reserve/PUP list by the Broncos on Sunday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: The offensive guard began camp on the active/PUP list and was never activated, prompting the move to reserve/PUP for the start of the regular season. Now, Gargiulo will have to miss at least the first four games of the 2026 campaign. The 2024 seventh-round pick should play a backup role once he's able to return.

injuries.name: Frank Crum
injuries.headline: Crum (undisclosed) was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return by the Broncos on Sunday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: The offensive tackle can return for Denver's Week 5 matchup with the Chargers at the earliest. Crum suffered a leg injury during the Broncos' second preseason against the Packers and missed the last week of training camp. The third-year pro projects as a depth tackle even when healthy.

injuries.name: Caleb Lohner
injuries.headline: Lohner (lower body) was placed on injured reserve by the Broncos on Sunday with a designation to return, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Lohner underwent a procedure in June to address a lower-body injury, and he remained sidelined throughout the preseason. The tight end will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the 2026 regular season, and the earliest he could make his season debut is in Week 5 against the Chargers on Oct. 11.

injuries.name: Troy Franklin
injuries.headline: Franklin failed to secure his only target in the Broncos' 34-6 preseason win over the Vikings on Friday.
injuries.notes: Franklin opened preseason with a 23-yard grab in the opener against the Falcons, but that turned out to be his only production of the exhibition slate across three games. Despite the quiet summer, Franklin is slated to serve as the No. 3 receiver behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle in what should be a high-powered Broncos air attack.

injuries.name: Evan Engram
injuries.headline: Engram played 16 snaps on offense but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Broncos' 33-13 preseason loss to the Packers on Friday.
injuries.notes: Engram was more involved offensively in the Broncos' preseason opener against the Falcons, when he caught one pass on three targets for 24 yards. He didn't see a target in Friday's exhibition game, and it remains to be seen whether Engram and the other Denver starters will play in the preseason finale against Minnesota this Friday. Engram is coming off a 2025 regular season in which he caught 50 passes on 76 targets for 461 yards and one touchdown across 16 games. He figures to lead the Broncos' tight end group that also includes Adam Trautman, Justin Joly and Nate Adkins.

injuries.name: Wil Lutz
injuries.headline: Lutz converted both field-goal attempts and made his sole extra-point try in Friday night's 33-13 preseason loss to the Packers.
injuries.notes: Lutz's seven points were over half of the Broncos' total scoring for the night. The kicker succeeded from 53 and 38 yards in the contest, continuing to prove he is the clear primary kicker for the team. Lutz made 28 of 32 field goals during 17 regular-season games in 2025, nailing four of six attempts from 50 yards or greater.

injuries.name: Levelle Bailey
injuries.headline: Bailey (leg) reverted to the Broncos' injured-reserve list Friday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
injuries.notes: Bailey will now spend the entirety of the 2026 campaign on injured reserve unless he is waived with an injury settlement. The linebacker sustained a broken leg in last Friday's preseason opener, so he will likely remain on the team's injured reserve for the season instead of settling.

injuries.name: Matt Henningsen
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Michael Deiter
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Nate Adkins
injuries.headline: Adkins (undisclosed) participated during the Broncos' training camp practice Monday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
injuries.notes: Adkins left practice with a trainer Friday after presumably suffering some type of injury, but it looks like it wasn't anything too serious. He'll continue to compete with the likes of rookie fifth-rounder Justin Joly and Lucas Krull for a depth role at tight end during the upcoming campaign.

injuries.name: D.J. Reed
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Isaac TeSlaa
injuries.headline: TeSlaa failed to haul in his only target during Detroit's overtime win over the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.notes: TeSlaa played 52 of the team's 77 offensive snaps but was still the only Lions player who didn't record any receptions, among those who were targeted. The 2025 third-round pick had a promising rookie campaign, catching 16 passes for 239 yards and six touchdowns despite limited usage, but he is coming off a disappointing training camp. TeSlaa will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 2 matchup against the Bills.

injuries.name: Jacob Saylors
injuries.headline: Saylors made one special-teams tackle and returned two kickoffs for 25 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win against the Saints.
injuries.notes: Saylors saw no offensive snaps in Sunday's contest, taking all 24 of his reps with the special-teams unit. Saylors made one tackle on kick coverage and had two short returns in the game, taking on most of the grunt work as the Lions' offense burned bright without him.

injuries.name: Sione Vaki
injuries.headline: Vaki turned two carries into seven yards while also reeling in his only target for 11 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win against New Orleans.
injuries.notes: Vaki operated as the Lions' No. 2 option running back in Week 1 behind starter Jahmyr Gibbs, but he didn't really have much of an impact over his 22 offensive snaps. The running back also logged 24 snaps on special teams in the victory. Gibbs will likely continue to dominate the touches in the backfield while Isiah Pacheco (back) is on injured reserve, leaving Vaki as an unappealing fantasy option.

injuries.name: Christian Izien
injuries.headline: Izien (groin) was considered to be a full participant at the Lions' walkthrough practice Monday.
injuries.notes: Izien was unavailable for the team's 31-30 overtime win against New Orleans on Sunday as a result of a groin issue, but he now appears to be on track to make his season debut in Week 2. The 26-year-old is expected to operate as a top reserve option behind Roger McCreary at slot cornerback, and his first test of the season will come Thursday night against the Bills.

injuries.name: Christian Mahogany
injuries.headline: Mahogany (knee) underwent imaging, which came back negative, following Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
injuries.notes: Mahogany suffered a lower-body injury in the first half of the team's Week 1 victory, and he was unable to return to the contest. The offensive lineman was ruled out with a knee injury, and the imaging results appear to have ruled out any significant damage to the knee. Head coach Dan Campbell explained that the offensive lineman isn't "out of the woods" quite yet though, stating that Mahogany may be dealing with a hip injury instead. The Lions are set to face the Bills on Thursday night in Buffalo, so Mahogany may have a tough time being available for Week 2.

injuries.name: Isiah Pacheco
injuries.headline: Pacheco (back) underwent surgery Monday and is expected to be out for a significant amount of time, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
injuries.notes: Pacheco was already on injured reserve, but he's looking at a lengthy recovery. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the running back is expected to be sidelined 12 weeks, giving him a "chance" to return sometime in December. With Pacheco sidelined Week 1 against the Saints, Jahmyr Gibbs handled 29 of the team's 31 backfield carries, turning them into 156 yards and two touchdowns. Gibbs also caught all five of his targets for 30 yards and played 57 of 77 offensive snaps. Sione Vaki played 22 snaps on offense but touched the ball just three times for 18 yards. Gibbs cemented himself as the premier player in fantasy football.

injuries.name: Blake Miller
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Juice Scruggs
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Jake Bates
injuries.headline: Bates made his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his extra-point tries in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
injuries.notes: Bates had a subpar 2025 season, converting just 27 of 34 field-goal tries and 54 of 56 PATs, and he followed it up with a rough preseason this summer. However, he was perfect against New Orleans, converting a chip-shot 23-yard field goal with the four extra points. Bates led all NFL kickers in point-after attempts and makes last season in Detroit's high-powered offense. If he can get his field-goal percentage back up closer to 90 percent, Bates should regain K1 status in fantasy this season.

injuries.name: Jameson Williams
injuries.headline: Williams gathered in just four of nine targets for 45 yards during Sunday's 31-30 overtime win against the Saints.
injuries.notes: QB Jared Goff and Williams weren't on the same page often Week 1, as the fifth-year wide receiver's catch rate fell below 50 percent, and nearly half of Williams' yards (22) occurred on one reception. Williams is coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard campaigns, a span in which he averaged 17.2 yards per grab, so he's a good bet to bounce back in the near future, and perhaps as soon as Thursday's road showdown with the Bills.

injuries.name: Sam LaPorta
injuries.headline: LaPorta caught five of eight targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
injuries.notes: The tight end finished second to Amon-Ra St. Brown in receiving yards on the day while tying Jahmyr Gibbs for second in catches. Back trouble limited LaPorta to just nine games in 2025, but his pace during those games would have resulted in a career-high 924 receiving yards, so staying healthy will be key to his fortunes this season. LaPorta will look to make a bigger impact in Week 2 on the road against the Bills.

injuries.name: Jared Goff
injuries.headline: Goff completed 26 of 39 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints. He added two yards on two carries.
injuries.notes: Both of Goff's TD passes went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, while Jahmyr Gibbs scored on a pair of one-yard runs. The Lions' offense may have gotten a little narrower in the offseason when David Montgomery left for the Texans, but that shouldn't affect the QB's production after he threw for at least 4,500 yards and 30 touchdowns in each of the last three seasons. Goff will now shift his focus to the Bills for a Week 2 road game.

injuries.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
injuries.headline: St. Brown caught 10 of 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
injuries.notes: The star wideout got the new season started with a bang, leading Detroit in catches, targets and receiving yards while connecting with Jared Goff for a 19-yard score in the third quarter and a four-yard strike in overtime. The latter proved to be the winning TD when New Orleans failed on a two-point attempt on its answering touchdown. St. Brown has scored double-digit TDs in three straight seasons, and he may be well on his way to doing so again. He'll look to make an impact again in Week 2 on the road against the Bills.

injuries.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
injuries.headline: Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the Saints.
injuries.notes: He did lose a fumble, but there wasn't much to criticize about Gibbs' performance otherwise. The star running back opened the scoring with a one-yard plunge in the first quarter, then added another one-yard TD on the Lions' first possession of the second half. Gibbs set a career high with 320 touches in 2025 (243 carries and 77 catches), but he could be headed for even bigger volume this season with David Montgomery no longer in Detroit to siphon away reps. Gibbs will look to keep rolling in Week 2 on the road against the Bills.

injuries.name: Penei Sewell
injuries.headline: The Lions restructured Sewell's contract Saturday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: The Lions converted $18.6 million of Sewell's contract into a signing bonus to free up cap space. The team also restructured the contract of Amon-Ra St. Brown, pointing to a potential move for either a high-value player or increased depth sometime soon.

injuries.name: Derrick Moore
injuries.headline: Moore (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus New Orleans.
injuries.notes: Moore was limited at practice earlier in the week with a hamstring issue, but he was able to log a full practice Friday and will be available in Week 1. Detroit used a second-round pick on the rookie back in April, so it wouldn't be surprising if he got significant playing time right away.

injuries.name: Tom Kennedy
injuries.headline: The Lions signed Kennedy from their practice squad to their active roster Thursday.
injuries.notes: Kennedy initially missed the cut for Detroit's 53-man roster for 2026, but he's now back in the fold with Week 1 looming. He could be tasked with punt-return duties Sunday versus the Saints.

injuries.name: Malcolm Rodriguez
injuries.headline: Rodriguez (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Rodriguez has recovered from the ankle injury he suffered in early August. The linebacker was not listed on the injury report and should be all set to suit up for Sunday's Week 1 contest against the Saints.

injuries.name: Cade Mays
injuries.headline: Mays (wrist) is looking to return from injured reserve by mid-October, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports.
injuries.notes: Mays was placed on IR during the Aug. 30 cutdown day. The center fractured his wrist during the preseason, but is eyeing a quick month and a half of downtime before being able to return to protecting Jared Goff. While Mays remains on IR, Juice Scruggs will be the starting safety for the Lions.

injuries.name: Trey Smack
injuries.headline: Smack made all three of his field-goal attempts while missing one of two PATs in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Smack made field goals from 59, 43 and 26 yards but fell short of a flawless night after missing an extra-point try. The sixth-round rookie had a strong debut overall with 10 total points.

injuries.name: Skyy Moore
injuries.headline: Moore failed to catch his only target and returned two punts for 17 yards during Green Bay's loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Moore saw the majority of his playing time on special teams, seeing 11 snaps compared to only four on offense. The 2022 second-round pick of the Chiefs will likely continue to serve as the Packers' primary returner going forward while seeing limited action on offense.

injuries.name: Kaleb Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson returned two kickoffs for 52 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Johnson played just two special-teams snaps in the contest, touching the ball on each. The third-string running back did not see a carry behind MarShawn Lloyd or Chris Brooks, but he may have earned a bigger role as a returner in a Week 2 matchup against the Jets.

injuries.name: Bo Melton
injuries.headline: The Packers signed Melton to the active roster Monday.
injuries.notes: Melton was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster for Sunday's loss to the Vikings. The wide receiver played 27 total snaps, catching his sole target for 10 yards on one of his seven offensive plays. The wide receiver played in 16 regular-season games for the Packers in 2025, logging four receptions for 107 yards and a touchdown as well as five rushing attempts for 35 yards.

injuries.name: Jonnu Smith
injuries.headline: Smith caught two of three targets for 50 yards in Sunday's Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Jordan Love wasn't shy about going to his tight ends, as Smith and Tucker Kraft combined for five catches and 115 yards. The bulk of Smith's production came on a 43-yard reception midway through the third quarter on which he was left wide open. Kraft is the clear No. 1 tight end in Green Bay, but Smith logged 32 of 68 offensive snaps Sunday and should chip in as a pass catcher most weeks. With that said, Smith is unlikely to be a trustworthy fantasy asset unless Kraft is sidelined at some point.

injuries.name: Chris Brooks
injuries.headline: Brooks turned seven carries into 29 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the Packers' 39-22 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
injuries.notes: With Josh Jacobs (personal) on the Commissioner's Exempt List to open the season, the Packers went with a one-two punch of Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd in the backfield. Brooks' 38 snaps on offense were ahead of Lloyd (30), though the latter led all Packers running backs with 13 carries for 37 yards. Neither RB managed to get anything going in the passing game, so the Packers may just ride the hot hand on a game-to-game basis while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers will stay on the road for their Week 2 matchup against the Jets on Sept. 20.

injuries.name: Matthew Golden
injuries.headline: Golden caught six of 12 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: With the Packers chasing the Vikings on the scoreboard much of the fourth quarter and getting virtually nothing from their running game all day, Jordan Love dropped back to pass 46 times, and Golden's 40 routes and 12 targets both led the team, as he lined up out wide 92.5 percent of the time. The second-year wideout's 28.6 percent target share is a great sign for his fantasy viability moving forward. Golden will be a WR3 with upside next Sunday on the road against the Jets.

injuries.name: MarShawn Lloyd
injuries.headline: Lloyd rushed 13 times for 37 yards and didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Lloyd worked ahead of Chris Brooks (seven carries for 29 yards) in a Packers backfield that struggled to generate much in the absence of Josh Jacobs (personal), who is on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Jordan Love threw 42 passes compared to 20 combined carries for Lloyd and Brooks, even though Green Bay led for most of the game prior to being outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter. Lloyd looks poised to handle double-digit touches again in Week 2 against the Jets.

injuries.name: Jordan Love
injuries.headline: Love completed 21 of 42 passes for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings. He also rushed once for no gain and fumbled twice, losing one.
injuries.notes: Love started hot, connecting with Christian Watson for an 81-yard touchdown in the first quarter and a two-yard touchdown in the final minute of the first half. Green Bay's offense sputtered in the second half, and both of Love's turnovers came in the fourth quarter, during which the Vikings outscored the Packers, 22-0. Love finished with the second-highest passing yards total of his career, trailing only his 389-yard performance in a Week 4 loss to the Vikings in 2024, and he exceeded 42 pass attempts only once in 15 regular-season starts last season. Green Bay may continue to rely heavily on Love's arm as long as Josh Jacobs (personal) is on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which may remain the case Week 2 against the Jets.

injuries.name: Tucker Kraft
injuries.headline: Kraft caught three of six targets for 65 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Kraft avoided the Week 1 injury report in his return from a torn ACL suffered Week 9 of last season. He finished third on the team in receiving yards in his return, behind wide receivers Christian Watson (147 yards) and Matthew Golden (95 yards). Kraft is poised to maintain a prominent role Week 2 against the Jets.

injuries.name: Jayden Reed
injuries.headline: Reed caught three of his seven targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Reed saw the third-most targets for the Packers behind Matthew Golden (12) and Christian Watson (eight), but the wide receiver could not haul in enough to match either's production. Tucker Kraft's 60 yards and Jonnu Smith's 50 yards also outproduced Reed on fewer targets, meaning Week 1 may not have instilled Jordan Love with much trust in the wide receiver.

injuries.name: Christian Watson
injuries.headline: Watson caught six of eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Watson broke free down the sideline for an 81-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter and added a two-yard touchdown catch to give the Packers a 19-10 lead with 14 seconds left in the first half. The Vikings dominated the second half as Green Bay's offense went quiet. Jordan Love threw the ball 42 times, and Watson could benefit if the Packers continue to employ pass-heavy game plans during the indefinite absence of starting running back Josh Jacobs (personal), who is on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Watson finished second on the team in targets Sunday behind Matthew Golden (12). The Packers will try to put this second-half collapse behind them in a Week 2 road game against the Jets.

injuries.name: Brandon Cisse
injuries.headline: Cisse (cramps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Cisse logged one solo tackle prior to his exit, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. Carrington Valentine will take over at outside corner opposite Keisean Nixon for as long as Cisse is out of the game.

injuries.name: Josh Whyle
injuries.headline: Whyle (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Whyle exited the second half of Sunday's contest with an all-too-familiar injury. The tight end missed some time in August with a minor neck issue so the current issue could be related. If Whyle is unable to return to the game, Mark Redman will likely take over as the No. 3 Packers tight end.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: Zach Bako-Bewele
injuries.headline: Bako-Bewele is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
injuries.notes: Bako-Bewele was listed as questionable Friday due to a knee injury. The offensive lineman is set to suit up opposite Jordan Morgan as the starting right tackle for Sunday's contest.

injuries.name: J. Michael Sturdivant
injuries.headline: Sturdivant (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
injuries.notes: The undrafted rookie out of Florida impressed the Packers' coaching staff enough to crack the 53-man roster at the end of training camp, but he'll have to wait until Week 2 against the Jets on Sunday, Sept. 20, to make his regular-season debut. Bo Melton and Skyy Moore will be the depth wideouts for Sunday's NFC North clash behind Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden.

injuries.name: Josh Jacobs
injuries.headline: Jacobs (personal) remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but the NFL may count time on the list as time served if it eventually issues a suspension to the running back, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Jacobs made an appearance in court Thursday and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property in a case stemming from a May domestic violence incident. There still are some moving parts related to the case, so it's unclear when exactly the NFL may issue a suspension, but Jacobs will continue to miss practices and games as long as he's on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

injuries.name: Devonte Wyatt
injuries.headline: Wyatt (ankle) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at Minnesota, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Wyatt was a limited participant at practice all week because of an issue with his ankle, but it looks like he'll be available in Week 1 anyway. Green Bay will be relying heavily on him to create disruption at the line of scrimmage in 2026, especially until Micah Parsons (knee) is back on the field.

injuries.name: Javon Hargrave
injuries.headline: Hargrave (knee) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at Minnesota, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Hargrave was limited at practice all week by a knee issue, but it won't keep him off the field in Week 1. To the extent that the veteran's stamina and health allows, he figures to see plenty of work on Green Bay's defensive line in 2026.

injuries.name: Jaylin Noel
injuries.headline: Noel recorded two catches for 53 yards and three kickoff returns for 70 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
injuries.notes: The wide receiver played on 24 of 79 offensive snaps and six more on special teams. Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte all played on more offensive snaps for the Texans. Noel, though, seems secure in his role as kick and punt returner, as he also had a fair catch on a punt during the defeat.

injuries.name: Henry To'oTo'o
injuries.headline: To'oTo'o might end up on injured reserve after hurting his shoulder during Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.notes: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that the team was still deciding on To'oTo'o's status. The linebacker was seen wearing a sling after the game. To'oTo'o suffered the injury late in the fourth quarter after playing 46 snaps.

injuries.name: Jake Hummel
injuries.headline: Hummel (groin) is considered week-to-week, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.notes: Hummel suffered a groin injury in the third quarter of Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills. The linebacker will almost certainly miss the Texans' Week 2 game against the Bengals. Jake Hansen will likely start as the second outside linebacker in Hummel's absence, but the team will probably rely on more nickel packages with Jalen Pitre in the slot while Hummel is absent.

injuries.name: Kayshon Boutte
injuries.headline: Boutte caught one of two targets for 21 yards in the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Acquired from the Patriots toward the end of training camp, Boutte is still in the process of building rapport with C.J. Stroud while learning the playbook. Boutte played behind both Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson against Buffalo, seeing just under 46 percent of the offensive snaps. Boutte's role could grow as the season goes along, but Hutchinson has long been a favorite of the coaching staff, and second-year WR Jaylin Noel also is in the mix for increased reps.

injuries.name: Xavier Hutchinson
injuries.headline: Hutchinson caught three passes (on six targets) for 32 yards during the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Hutchinson finished third among Texans pass catchers in both targets and receptions, including a 20-yard catch late in the fourth quarter. His 44 snaps on offense were second-most among wide receivers behind Nico Collins (57), suggesting that Hutchinson is the Texans' WR2 ahead of Kayshoun Boutte (36 snaps) and Jaylin Noel (24 snaps) in the absence of Jayden Higgins (knee, IR). The Texans will stay at home for Week 2 against the Bengals on Sept. 20.

injuries.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
injuries.headline: Fairbairn made his lone field-goal attempt and all four PATs in Sunday's 36-31 loss to Buffalo.
injuries.notes: Fairbairn's field goal was drilled from 58 yards in the fourth quarter to bring the Texans within one point. Fantasy's No. 1 overall kicker last season, Fairbairn has had a mistake-free 2026 to this point after he went perfect during the preseason. The 32-year-old led the NFL in field-goal attempts (48) and makes (44) last season, while also converting all 28 of his extra-point tries.

injuries.name: Dalton Schultz
injuries.headline: Schultz caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
injuries.notes: Schultz's eight targets were second on the team to Nico Collins' 10 on 38 pass attempts by C.J. Stroud. Schultz doesn't offer much big-play ability at 30 years old, but he's a reliable target in the middle of the field and saw his floor raise when Jayden Higgins went down with a season-ending torn ACL over the summer. The veteran tight end will be a borderline TE1/2 next Sunday against the Bengals.

injuries.name: Woody Marks
injuries.headline: Marks rushed nine times for 42 yards and caught his lone target for a two-yard loss in the Texans' 36-31 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injuries.notes: While David Montgomery stole the headlines with three total touchdowns, Montgomery wasn't exactly efficient with his 20 carries, turning them into just 60 yards (3.0 YPC). Marks averaged 4.7 yards per carry with his nine attempts and actually out-snapped his veteran backfield mate 40 to 39 and ran 20 routes to Montgomery's 14, proving the 50-50 split talk from the summer to be true in the season opener. Marks remains an elite fantasy bench stash with some standalone value as an RB3 during bye weeks.

injuries.name: C.J. Stroud
injuries.headline: Stroud completed 26 of 38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills. He also rushed twice for 15 yards and fumbled twice, losing both fumbles.
injuries.notes: Stroud guided a pair of touchdown drives capped by David Montgomery runs before finding Nico Collins for a 12-yard touchdown in the final minute of the first half. The 24-year-old QB gave the Texans a one-point lead with a seven-yard touchdown pass to Montgomery in the fourth quarter, but the Bills responded with a 9-3 run to take a five-point lead with 1:36 remaining. Houston's final drive got to first-and-goal at Buffalo's nine-yard line before Stroud took two sacks in a three-play span, the last of which ended in his second lost fumble of the game. Turnovers in big moments have become a recurring issue for Stroud, who turned the ball over seven times in two games last postseason. Stroud and the Texans will try to bounce back in Week 2 against the Bengals.

injuries.name: Nico Collins
injuries.headline: Collins caught seven of 10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown while adding a seven-yard run in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
injuries.notes: C.J. Stroud connected with Collins for a 12-yard touchdown in the second quarter, marking the first touchdown of the season for both Houston's quarterback and the team's star wide receiver. Collins led the Texans in targets, catches and receiving yards Sunday after finishing as Houston's receiving yards leader in each of the previous three regular seasons. He is locked in as Stroud's top target heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals.

injuries.name: David Montgomery
injuries.headline: Montgomery rushed 20 times for 60 yards and two touchdowns while catching all three of his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
injuries.notes: Montgomery scored Houston's first two touchdowns of the season with a one-yard run in the first quarter followed by an 18-yard run in the second. The offseason trade acquisition from Detroit added a third touchdown on a seven-yard catch as the Texans pulled ahead 28-27 early in the fourth quarter, but Houston's vaunted defense failed to hold that lead. Montgomery's 23 touches in his Texans debut were more than he had in any of his 17 regular-season appearances in 2025 for Detroit, where he had to share the backfield with Jahmyr Gibbs. Woody Marks had 10 touches for 40 yards in a change-of-pace role behind Montgomery, but the latter is clearly Houston's top running back heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals.

injuries.name: Kayden McDonald
injuries.headline: The Texans placed McDonald (ankle) on injured reserve Friday.
injuries.notes: McDonald was limited in practice Wednesday and missed practice Thursday, suggesting he suffered the injury in practice this week. He'll now be required to miss at least the first four games of the season. Logan Hall, Mario Edwards and Jaden Crumedy will see the rotational snaps at defensive tackle behind Tommy Togiai and Sheldon Rankins.

injuries.name: Dominique Robinson
injuries.headline: Robinson (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Robinson injured his calf during the Texans' preseason contest with the Raiders in mid-August. The defensive end was released by the Texans on Aug. 30 but promptly re-signed with the team on a one-year, $4 million deal. The 28-year-old has recovered from the calf injury just in time for Sunday's home opener against the Bills.

injuries.name: Jake Hansen
injuries.headline: Hansen (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: Hansen was carted off the field at the start of training camp in late July with an ankle issue. The linebacker was listed as week-to-week as he managed the injury and has finally recovered just in time for the Texans' Week 1 showdown with the Bills.

injuries.name: Wade Woodaz
injuries.headline: Woodaz (thumb) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Woodaz broke his thumb during the Texans' preseason game at Las Vegas in August, but it doesn't look like that will keep him out in Week 1 versus the Bills. The rookie fourth-rounder projects to start his career in a rotational role at linebacker.

injuries.name: Jadeveon Clowney
injuries.headline: Clowney (hip/ankle) was not listed on Houston's official injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Clowney sustained a soft-tissue injury to his hip during the Texans' preseason game at Las Vegas, but it appears he'll be available for Week 1. The veteran figures to settle into a rotational role on the edge behind All-Pro Will Anderson and five-time Pro Bowler Danielle Hunter.

injuries.name: British Brooks
injuries.headline: Brooks (hand) was not listed on Houston's official injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Brooks broke his hand during a practice back in early August, but it doesn't look like it's holding him back anymore. He's not likely to see many snaps on offense in Week 1, barring an injury to David Montgomery or Woody Marks.

injuries.name: Jayden Higgins
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Tank Dell
injuries.headline: Dell (knee) agreed to take a pay cut from the Texans on Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.notes: Entering the final year of his rookie deal, Dell was scheduled to collect $3.624 million, but he'll now make just over $1.7 million in 2026. Dell missed the entirety of the 2025 campaign after a catastrophic knee injury suffered toward the end of the previous season. He's now opening this season on injured reserve and won't be eligible to play until Week 5 at the earliest.

injuries.name: Austin Ajiake
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Spencer Shrader
injuries.headline: Shrader converted his only field-goal attempt and two of his three extra-point tries during Indianapolis' loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Shrader's lone make came from 58 yards out, which was a new career long for the 27-year-old. He spent time with three different teams across the last two seasons before beating out Blake Grupe for the Colts' kicking job during training camp, and Shrader will look to keep producing as the season goes on.

injuries.name: Cam Taylor-Britt
injuries.headline: Taylor-Britt's one-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy was lifted Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.notes: Taylor-Britt was forced to sit out Indianapolis' Week 1 loss to the Ravens, but he's now on track to be available for Week 2 at Kansas City. He figures to play in a rotational role in the Colts' secondary in 2026.

injuries.name: Seth McGowan
injuries.headline: McGowan caught his only target for no gain and notched 164 yards on five kickoff returns during Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: McGowan was only on the field for six of the team's 54 offensive snaps while operating as the top reserve option at running back behind Jonathan Taylor. McGowan definitely made his mark on special teams during the contest, but as long as Taylor is healthy, the former will likely have a limited impact on offense.

injuries.name: Keenan Allen
injuries.headline: Allen caught all six of his targets for 32 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Allen played 36 of 54 offensive snaps against Baltimore and ran 26 routes on Daniel Jones' 34 dropbacks. He ran six fewer routes than Josh Downs, but Allen's microscopic 3.7-yard average depth of target made him an easy pitch-and-catch option for the quarterback. Allen lacks explosiveness at this stage of his career, but he's always been able to earn targets. He's a low-floor fantasy option at 34 years old.

injuries.name: Alec Pierce
injuries.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that Pierce is "good right now" after banging up his wrist in Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: After undergoing offseason ankle surgery and missing most of training camp, Pierce was expected to have his snaps limited to some degree in Week 1. He ended up finishing with four receptions for 61 yards on six targets while taking the field for 32 of the Colts' 54 snaps, but it's unclear what affect the wrist issue may have had on his workload. With X-rays on Pierce's left hand having already returned negative, Pierce is expected to be ready to play in the Colts' Week 2 contest in Kansas City, though he may not necessarily be a full participant in all of the team's practices leading up to game day.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Josh Downs
injuries.headline: Downs caught two of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Downs' four targets tied Jonathan Taylor for fourth on the team behind Alec Pierce (six), Keenan Allen (six) and Tyler Warren (five), but it was notable that Downs led the team with 32 routes on Daniel Jones' 34 dropbacks. He was in the slot 78.8 percent of the time, and his 93.8 percent route participation suggests Downs is an every-down wideout this season after playing behind both Michael Pittman and Pierce in previous seasons. Downs should have better days moving forward and gets a Week 2 date with the Chiefs next Sunday.

injuries.name: Daniel Jones
injuries.headline: Jones completed 19 of 31 passes for 166 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding one rush for four yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Jones' middling final line underscored the type of afternoon it was for the Colts' offense overall, which largely struggled outside of some typically strong play on the part of Jonathan Taylor. Jones averaged only 5.4 yards per attempt and took two sacks while finishing with a paltry QB rating of 28.7. The one highlight of Jones' day came late, as he hit Tyler Warren for a nine-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter. Jones may progressively look better the further removed he is from last year's Achilles tear, but he has another tough assignment in Week 2 on the road against the Chiefs next Sunday night.

injuries.name: Tyler Warren
injuries.headline: Warren secured three of five targets for 13 yards and a touchdown in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The athletic second-year tight end was on the receiving end of Daniel Jones' sole touchdown pass, recording his nine-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter. Warren's afternoon was otherwise as non-descript as his final line suggests, but he's a vital part of the Colts' air attack and could have a bigger role in a Week 2 road matchup against the Chiefs next Sunday night.

injuries.name: Jonathan Taylor
injuries.headline: Taylor rushed 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Ravens on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.notes: Taylor and the Colts' offense as a whole got the new season off to a highly encouraging start, capping off a crisp opening drive with the star running back's one-yard touchdown run. Taylor would go on to add a three-yard scoring rush late in the first half after the Ravens had gone on to rattle off 28 straight points, with Taylor's fumble after a 14-yard reception leading to one of Baltimore's touchdowns. Outside of the turnover, Taylor's overall numbers in a game during which his rushing opportunities were capped late were still useful for fantasy managers, and he'll be slated for another prominent role in a Week 2 road showdown against the Chiefs next Sunday night.

injuries.name: Drew Ogletree
injuries.headline: Ogletree (neck) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: The tight end was limited by a neck injury a day earlier. Ogletree is trending toward playing in Sunday's opener against Baltimore. The 2022 sixth-round pick has added depth to the Colts' tight-end spot throughout his career, seeing action on special teams as well.

injuries.name: A.J. Haulcy
injuries.headline: Haulcy (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.notes: The safety missed the Colts' last two preseason games but was able to practice on a limited basis Wednesday. Now that he's a full go in practice, Haulcy should be able to play Sunday against the Ravens. The third-round pick out of LSU is a projected starter at strong safety.

injuries.name: Sauce Gardner
injuries.headline: Gardner (calf) is not listed on Wednesday's injury report for Sunday's game versus Baltimore.
injuries.notes: Gardner was bothered by a calf issue during the preseason. However, his omission from the injury report indicates he will be good to go for the Week 1 meeting with the Ravens. The 2022 No. 4 overall pick appeared in 11 regular-season games for the Jets and Colts during the 2025 campaign, amassing 36 total tackles and nine passes defended.

injuries.name: Charvarius Ward
injuries.headline: Ward (back) was not listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday's game versus the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Ward was battling a back injury. However, his absence from Wednesday's injury report indicates he should be good to go for the opener versus Baltimore. The 30-year-old veteran appeared in seven regular-season games for the Colts during the 2025 campaign, compiling 25 total tackles.

injuries.name: Carson Towt
injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir

injuries.name: Sean McKeon
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Anthony Richardson Sr.
injuries.headline: Richardson will open the season as the Colts' backup quarterback, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
injuries.notes: GM Chris Ballard confirmed Tuesday that Richardson -- who requested a trade over the offseason -- would remain with the Colts for the season, and head coach Shane Steichen revealed Thursday that Richardson beat out Riley Leonard for the backup job behind starter Daniel Jones.

injuries.name: D.J. Montgomery
injuries.headline: Montgomery (abdomen) was placed on injured reserve by the Colts on Sunday, JJ Stankevitz of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Montgomery signed with the team in early August, ultimately reeling in two of three targets for 21 yards during the preseason. The wide receiver appears to have picked up an abdominal injury at some point during the preseason, and he is now set to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he reaches an injury settlement with Indianapolis.

injuries.name: Will Mallory
injuries.headline: Mallory (thumb) was placed on injured reserve by the Colts on Sunday with a designation to return, JJ Stankevitz of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Mallory suffered a thumb injury, and he sat out the team's last two games of the preseason. The tight end will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the 2026 campaign, and the earliest he'll be able to make his regular-season debut is in Week 5 against the Steelers on Oct. 11.

injuries.name: Rigoberto Sanchez
injuries.headline: Sanchez signed an extension through 2028 with the Colts on Thursday, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Sanchez is entering his 10th season as the Colts' primary punter and kickoff specialist. He enjoyed a career season in 2025, landing 50 percent of his punts inside the 20 and recording a 44.7-yard net average, the second-best mark in the league.

injuries.name: CJ Williams
injuries.headline: Williams didn't record any offensive stats during Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
injuries.notes: Williams had a quiet outing during his regular-season debut, failing to record any targets across 10 offensive snaps. The rookie sixth-round pick also played six snaps on special teams and will likely continue to see limited usage going forward.

injuries.name: Nate Boerkircher
injuries.headline: Boerkircher caught his only target for nine yards during Sunday's 34-10 win versus the Browns.
injuries.notes: Boerkircher played 38 of Jacksonville's 57 offensive snaps in his pro debut, good for second most among Jaguars tight ends behind Brenton Strange (39). Boerkircher was billed as more of a blocker than a route runner when he was taken in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and at least in the short term, Strange should be expected to continue to see more targets between the two of them.

injuries.name: LeQuint Allen Jr.
injuries.headline: Allen played one offensive snap and didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
injuries.notes: The 2025 seventh-rounder was cleared to play Week 1 after being limited by a hip injury, but he was an afterthought in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten (28 snaps), Chris Rodriguez (23) and Ameer Abdullah (five). Perhaps the hip was still an issue for Allen, but he's unlikely to see much playing time on offense unless Tuten or Rodriguez were to miss time.

injuries.name: Josh Cameron
injuries.headline: Cameron caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The sixth-round rookie wideout played well ahead of Travis Hunter, out-snapping him by a 19-4 margin behind the Jaguars' top trio of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas and Jakobi Meyers at wideout. Cameron ended up catching Trevor Lawrence's second touchdown, a four-yard score toward the end of the first quarter. Cameron would appear to have the lead for WR4 duties in Jacksonville.

injuries.name: Travis Hunter
injuries.headline: Hunter played four offensive snaps in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: On those four plays, Hunter recorded an eight-yard catch on one target and rushed for three yards on one carry. On defense, Hunter logged 29 snaps and totaled one solo tackle. It's become evident that the Jaguars have no plans to feature Hunter on offense unless the wide-receiver room is struck by a string of injuries. He can be left on the waiver wire in all redraft fantasy formats.

injuries.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
injuries.headline: Coach Liam Coen said Monday that Thomas (shoulder) will be limited in practice this week, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Thomas was briefly forced from Sunday's win over the Browns but was able to return and finished with three catches for 40 yards on three targets. Coen expects Thomas to play next Sunday against the Broncos despite the shoulder issue, but the matchup will be much tougher on paper. Behind Parker Washington in the pecking order for targets, Thomas is shaping up as a WR4 fantasy bet moving forward.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Cam Little
injuries.headline: Little went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
injuries.notes: After finishing as fantasy's K5 overall last regular season, Little picked up right where he left off in Week 1 against Cleveland. His field-goal makes came from 47 and 40 yards Sunday, and he's now 31-for-37 on field goals from 40-plus yards out across 35 career regular-season contests. The big-legged Little is an every-week K1 in this Jacksonville offense.

injuries.name: Brenton Strange
injuries.headline: Strange caught two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown Sunday in a 34-10 victory versus Cleveland.
injuries.notes: Strange had a relatively quiet day in terms of targets and yardage, but he finished with a fine fantasy total on the strength of a 14-yard connection with Trevor Lawrence in the second quarter. Strange seems to have carried over the red-zone chemistry with Lawrence that developed late last year, when all three of his scores came over the Jaguars' final six regular-season games. The 2023 second-round draft pick logged a career-best 540 receiving yards last season and is positioned to be Jacksonville's top tight end again in 2026.

injuries.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
injuries.headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
injuries.notes: Bhayshul Tuten got the start and out-snapped Rodriguez by a 28-23 margin and out-carried him 15 to six in one of the friendliest rushing environments the Jaguars will see all season after Jacksonville jumped out to a 31-0 lead early in the third quarter. The lack of volume and production from Rodriguez in this spot is concerning for his fantasy viability moving forward, as Tuten seemed to have the clear upper hand and averaged 4.4 yards per carry to Rodriguez's 3.8 mark. Tuten also caught a 22-yard pass, while Rodriguez didn't see a target. It was clear against Cleveland that Tuten is the preferred fantasy option in this backfield.

injuries.name: Parker Washington
injuries.headline: Washington secured five of six targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also returned one punt for minus-5 yards.
injuries.notes: Washington led the Jaguars in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his impressive 30-yard touchdown grab in the first quarter kicked off a prolific afternoon for Jacksonville's offense. Washington, whose late-season surge in 2025 has put him in line for an extension, certainly benefits from the strong start to the new season in that regard, and he should remain a focal point despite a tough Week 2 road matchup against the Broncos next Sunday.

injuries.name: Jakobi Meyers
injuries.headline: Meyers caught both of his targets for 40 total yards and a touchdown, adding one carry for two yards in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
injuries.notes: Meyers did not receive much attention despite a strong offensive day for the Jaguars. Parker Washington earned No. 1 option honors, catching five passes for 83 yards and a touchdown, while Meyers took a more minimal yet efficient role with 20 yards per reception.

injuries.name: Trevor Lawrence
injuries.headline: Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 245 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for two yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Lawrence's afternoon was about as smooth as his numbers suggest, as he helped stake the Jaguars to a 24-0 halftime lead with a trio of touchdown tosses to Parker Washington (30 yards), Josh Cameron (four yards) and Brenton Strange (14 yards). Lawrence added a 32-yard scoring strike to Jakobi Meyers to cap off the opening possession of the second half, and the air attack didn't need to do much more heavy lifting from that point on after the TD extended Jacksonville's lead to 31-0. Lawrence gets a much stiffer test in Week 2, however, as the Jaguars pay a visit to the Broncos next Sunday afternoon.

injuries.name: Bhayshul Tuten
injuries.headline: Tuten rushed 15 times for 66 yards and brought in his only target for 22 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
injuries.notes: Any questions surrounding the potential workload split in the Jaguars' ground attack were definitively answered for the time being Sunday, as Tuten put together an impressively efficient performance and outpaced backfield mate Chris Rodriguez by nine carries despite seeing his day come to an early end due to the lopsided score. Tuten was able to consistently generate productive runs, but he'll have a much stiffer test on the road against the Broncos in a Week 2 matchup next Sunday.

injuries.name: B.J. Green II
injuries.headline: Green (elbow) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuries.notes: Green injured his elbow while on punt coverage in the first quarter, and the injury is severe enough that he won't return to Sunday's contest. Danny Striggow will be the primary rotational option at defensive end behind Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker in Green's absence.

injuries.name: Tanner Koziol
injuries.headline: Koziol (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuries.notes: Koziol, the Jaguars' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, will be a healthy inactive for Week 1, so his next chance to make his regular-season debut is Week 2 against the Broncos on Sunday, Sept. 20. Brenton Strange, Quintin Morris and rookie second-rounder Nate Boerkircher will be Jacksonville's active tight ends against Cleveland.

injuries.name: Quinn Ewers
injuries.headline: Ewers (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuries.notes: The Jaguars traded for Ewers toward the tail end of training camp, but the 2025 seventh-rounder will be a healthy scratch Week 1 while Nick Mullens serves as Jacksonville's backup QB behind Trevor Lawrence. Ewers isn't listed as the emergency third quarterback against Cleveland, so his next chance to suit up is Week 2 against Denver on Sunday, Sept. 20.

injuries.name: Cole Van Lanen
injuries.headline: Van Lanen (knee) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Browns, Mia O'Brien of 1010 XL 92.5 FM Jacksonville reports.
injuries.notes: Van Lanen was limited in practice all week but has been cleared to face Cleveland. He was limited throughout training camp but appears ready to go as the Jaguars' starting right tackle.

injuries.name: Wyatt Milum
injuries.headline: Milum (undisclosed) was not listed on Wednesday's injury report.
injuries.notes: Milum was working through an unspecified injury during the last couple of weeks of training camp, but his absence from Wednesday's report puts him on track to play against the Browns in Sunday's regular-season opener. Milum provides the Jaguars with depth on the offensive line for the 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: Ameer Abdullah
injuries.headline: Abdullah earned a spot on the Jaguars' 53-man roster following a strong training camp, John Oehser of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Abdullah and LeQuint Allen (undisclosed) will enter the regular season as the rotational running backs behind co-starters Bhayshul Tuten (illness) and Chris Rodriguez. Abdullah played in only one of the Jaguars' three preseason games, but he did enough during training camp and joint practices to crack the 53-man roster for the 2026 campaign. The 2015 second-rounder appeared in 13 regular-season games for the Colts last year, finishing with 14 carries for 60 yards and a touchdown along with 16 catches (on 17 targets) for 99 yards.

injuries.name: Sam Mustipher
injuries.headline: The Jaguars placed Mustipher (undisclosed) on injured reserve Sunday.
injuries.notes: The move to IR does not come with a designation to return, meaning Mustipher will be forced to miss the entire 2026 season. It's unclear when he sustained the injury or what the nature of it is, but he'll shift his focus toward being fully healthy for the 2027 campaign.

injuries.name: Patrick Mekari
injuries.headline: The Jaguars placed Mekari (back) on injured reserve with a designation to return Sunday.
injuries.notes: Mekari will be required to miss at least the first four games of the regular season, meaning Week 5 against the Eagles on Sunday, Oct. 11 is the earliest he can play. The California product is recovering from back surgery that he underwent in mid-August. Ezra Cleveland is in line to start at right guard for as long as Mekari is out of action.

injuries.name: Emmett Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson rushed eight times for 24 yards in the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night. He added two catches for 44 yards on two targets.
injuries.notes: The rookie won the RB2 job behind Kenneth Walker pretty convincingly during training camp and the preseason, and Johnson showed why against Denver, consistently making plays with the ball in his hands. Most of his work came late in the fourth quarter with the game out of hand, but it's evident Johnson is a premier bench stash in fantasy should something happen to Walker.

injuries.name: Xavier Worthy
injuries.headline: Worthy secured three of six targets for 18 yards in the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Worthy was on the receiving end of Patrick Mahomes' first completion of the season, which went for nine yards and took the Chiefs down to the Broncos' 26-yard line on an opening drive that culminated in a 15-yard touchdown run by the returning signal-caller. Worthy produced modest gains on his other pair of grabs, but Mahomes recorded just five completions overall to wide receivers in the season-opening victory. Worthy boasts the potential for much better production, and he could have a good opportunity to deliver on that upside in a favorable Week 2 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday night.

injuries.name: Travis Kelce
injuries.headline: Kelce brought in three of five targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Kelce comfortably paced the Chiefs in receiving yards while tying for the team lead in receptions and finishing as the runner-up in targets.
